te: Subcommittees' work: relief for state officials accused unfairly, interference in cases through online media, and dog control
se: The meeting noted the work of all 3 subcommittees: Justice (approaches to helping and providing relief to state officials who are accused and investigated unfairly); Legal Affairs (interference in the justice process through social media, enforcement of the dog control law, and spreading knowledge of new laws); and Police Affairs (petitions, and a case appearing in online media of alleged demands for benefits in Nakhon Si Thammarat Province, with the Royal Thai Police invited to clarify). It also considered the schedule of bilateral meetings abroad
it: Subcommittee on Justice: approaches to helping and providing relief to state officials who are accused and subjected to inquiries unfairly
Subcommittee on Legal Affairs: interference in the justice process through social media · enforcement of the dog control law · spreading knowledge of new laws
Subcommittee on Police Affairs: petitions, and a case appearing in online media of alleged demands for benefits in Nakhon Si Thammarat Province (Royal Thai Police invited)
Schedule of bilateral meetings and visits abroad
Appointment of persons to positions in the committee

te: Online goods not as advertised: OCPB, TISI, FDA and CIB invited to give information
se: The meeting considered the problem of goods and services sold not as described in advertising, especially online, which may violate consumer rights, inviting the Office of the Consumer Protection Board, the Thai Industrial Standards Institute, the Food and Drug Administration and the Central Investigation Bureau to give information. It also planned study visits to the Department of Corrections and to Udon Thani and Nong Khai Provinces
cre: Second Vice-Chair of the committee, presiding over the meeting
it: Goods and services not as advertised, especially in online sales (OCPB, TISI, FDA and the Central Investigation Bureau invited)
Study visit and exchange of views at the Department of Corrections, Ministry of Justice
Schedule of the study visit to Udon Thani and Nong Khai Provinces
Appointment of persons to positions in the committee

te: A petition on frequency bands, a news report concerning the Office of the NACC, and preventing the exploitation of tourists
se: The meeting noted the work of its subcommittees and considered petitions from the public, including a petition asking for checks on the Office of the NBTC's payment of compensation for reclaiming the 2500–2690 MHz frequency band. It considered news reports in the media of allegations of bribery connected with the Office of the NACC (allegations as reported in the news, not a conclusion), and began studying approaches to improving the law to prevent the exploitation of tourists
it: Petition asking for checks on the payment of compensation for reclaiming the 2500–2690 MHz frequency band (as alleged by the petitioner)
News reports in the media of allegations of bribery connected with the Office of the NACC (allegations as reported in the news, not a conclusion)
Study of, and recommendations on, approaches to improving the law to prevent the exploitation of tourists
Appointment of persons to positions in the committee

te: Work in 2026 begins: 2 petitions, and the Royal Thai Police's explanation of a case in the news noted
se: At the first meeting of 2026 (7 Jan 2026), the meeting noted the relevant Cabinet resolutions and the work of its subcommittees, considered 2 petitions from the public, and noted the Royal Thai Police's written explanation of a case reported in the news in which police officers changed their testimony in a case, which the committee will keep for use in its further study
it: Cabinet resolutions relevant to the committee's work
Work of the Subcommittees on Legal Affairs, Justice and Police Affairs
Preventing and solving technology crime: the case reported in the news in which police officers changed their testimony in a case (explained in a document from the Royal Thai Police)
